It makes soju and gin and serves anju, small dishes meant to go with drinks, the list said. Menu prices run from $7 for olives to $25 for braised short rib, according to the report.

In Back Bay, Shuden Bar operates as a weekly pop-up on Wednesdays from 4 to 9 p.m. at The Irving, inside The Lenox at 61 Exeter St. It serves hand-rolled sushi and Japanese whiskies, according to Boston.com.

Also in Back Bay, Zhu has opened in soft-opening mode at 903 Boylston St., the former Lir space, the list said. Chef Joanna Zhu's three-level restaurant has an open dim sum bar, dumplings and handmade noodles with lobster, Boston.com reported.

globe-weekend-guide-for-sept-25-27.title: Jonas Brothers, Porchfest and 'Wicked' Top Boston's Sept. 25-27 Weekend
globe-weekend-guide-for-sept-25-27.dek: The Boston Globe's weekend guide lists concerts, comedy, festivals, theater and museum openings around the region for Sept. 25 through 27.
body: The Boston Globe's guide to the weekend of Sept. 25 to 27 highlighted, among other events, the Jonas Brothers at TD Garden, the Sam Adams Octoberfest and Brookline Porchfest.

The Jonas Brothers were scheduled to play TD Garden on Friday, Sept. 25, at 7:30 p.m., with tickets from $69, according to the guide. Role Model was set to perform at Leader Bank Pavilion on Sunday, Sept. 27, with Samia opening. Comedian Craig Robinson had four shows at Laugh Boston on Friday and Saturday, the Globe reported.

The Samuel Adams Boston Brewery, 30 Germania St., was holding its Octoberfest all weekend, with tickets from $10. Brookline Porchfest offered free performances across the town on Saturday from 11 a.m. to 6:30 p.m., with a rain date of Oct. 3, the guide said. A free a cappella festival with more than 15 groups was planned for Saturday at the Riverstage at Herter Park in Allston.

In theater, "Wicked" opened the Broadway in Boston season at the Citizens Opera House and runs through Nov. 15, according to the Globe. The paper's critics also recommended Arthur Miller's "All My Sons" at Lyric Stage, York Walker's "Covenant" at SpeakEasy Stage, and Rossini's "William Tell," Boston Lyric Opera's 50th-season opener, at the Emerson Colonial Theatre.

The Boston Symphony Orchestra, under Andris Nelsons, was performing Mahler's Symphony No. 7 on Sept. 25 and 26, and the MFA was opening a retrospective of artist Suzanne Jackson on Sept. 26, the guide said. Lucy Raven's exhibition at the ICA Watershed was set to close on Sept. 27.

twa-hotel-hosts-three-day-mission-60s-sp.title: TWA Hotel Hosts Three-Day 'Mission: 60s' Space Event at JFK
twa-hotel-hosts-three-day-mission-60s-sp.dek: The weekend event, running Oct. 23 through Oct. 25, brings former astronauts, an Apollo flight director and a Star Trek actor to the TWA Hotel.
body: The TWA Hotel at JFK Airport will host Mission: 60s, a three-day event on Apollo, aviation and 1960s space culture, from Friday, Oct. 23, through Sunday, Hoodline reported. Organizers say the event bridges the Apollo and Artemis eras of spaceflight.
The organizers are Luna Replicas, which sells vintage space gear, and Space for Humanity, a nonprofit that funds spaceflight for people who are not professional astronauts, according to Hoodline.

Scheduled speakers include Apollo flight director Gerry Griffin, Time science editor Jeffrey Kluger, former NASA astronauts Nicole Stott and Ron Garan, Star Trek actor Bob Picardo and researcher Frank White. Panels over the weekend cover Apollo mission control, women in aerospace, lunar communications, science fiction and space advocacy. Uplift Aerospace will run a shared virtual reality experience for up to 50 people. A Sunday keynote will focus on NASA's Artemis program.

Friday's program includes a guided trip to the site of the 1964 World's Fair in Flushing Meadows, where the New York Hall of Science's Rocket Park displays a Mercury-Atlas D, a Gemini-Titan II booster and a Saturn V F-1 engine. On Saturday, a gathering will be held aboard the hotel's restored 1958 Lockheed Constellation, now a cocktail lounge, with live music by Bonnie Gordon. A vendor hall is open both days.

A full-weekend pass is $150 and single-day admission is $85, with add-ons for VIP access, galas and the Friday excursion, according to Hoodline. The hotel occupies Eero Saarinen's TWA Flight Center, which opened in 1962 and reopened as a hotel in 2019.
